newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, Minas discount tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, Minas discount tumbles.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady in outright terms on Thursday but crudes across the board were trading at deeper discounts to their official selling prices.
One Japanese refiner reported it had purchased Indonesia's Minas crude oil as low as ICP -50 cents, by far the lowest traded level for March barrels so far.
Up to now traders had assessed Minas at a discount of five to 15 cents, although they had expected prices to come under further pressure owing to the lack of apparent buyers.
The fate of Minas followed the sharp decline in Duri crude, which has fallen to trade in recent days at ICP -30 cents.
Both crudes are in good supply owing to the maintenance shutdown of the 120,000 bpd Dumai refinery last weekend for 38 days. Dumai uses Minas for about 70 percent of its feedstock and Duri the rest.
MidEast grades showed further weakness also, with Oman trading several times. Japanese players traded 150,000 barrels of Oman at MPM -6.5 cents, the lowest deal to date.
Further ADNOC and Qatar deals emerged, but at deeper discounts.
Murban was heard traded at ADNOC -14 cents from a Japanese refiner to a European major. Qatar Marine traded at QGPC -22 cents, reflecting a recent deal at QGPC -25 cents.
Lower Zakum traded between Japanese players at ADNOC -10 cents, although traders said they believed the deal was a few days old.
Paper numbers were generally steady with Brent Dubai and Dubai intermonths spreads waiting on a direction from Brent futures.
